requirements.requirement: Each cell has a bin that drains
requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:2,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain — all 'full depth, drained' variant with drainage holes
All three bins filled to rim with soil and planted: prop:4 basil-young, prop:5 mint-young, prop:6 parsley-young; visible in look from 45°

finish.summary: Built a linear three-cell planter with a drained full-depth bin in each cell, capped open faces and locked joints, then filled with soil and planted with basil, mint and parsley to show herb use.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Three side-by-side cells, each with its own draining bin — I'll lay out your herb planter.
